title: A neighborhood reading room
description: A sample interview about a shared space for books, conversation, and quiet time. These are demonstration answers, not project decisions.

questions.title: What should the room feel like on an ordinary afternoon?
questions.context: Imagine someone walking in with an hour to spare. Choose the experience we should design around first.

options.label: A quiet place to settle in
options.description: Comfortable seats, individual reading spots, and a shared expectation of quiet. People can be together without needing to join in.
options.benefit: A dependable retreat for reading and focused work.
options.tradeoff: Spontaneous conversations need a separate space or time.

options.label: A place to meet over books
options.description: A large shared table and an easygoing atmosphere where conversations are welcome. Reading becomes a way to get to know neighbors.
options.benefit: Makes it easier for newcomers to connect with people.
options.tradeoff: Noise and interruptions can make longer reading sessions difficult.

options.label: A little of both, in separate zones
options.description: A quiet reading area alongside a smaller conversation area, with furniture and signs making the difference clear.
options.benefit: Accommodates different moods and reasons for visiting.
options.tradeoff: Needs more space and careful attention to sound carrying between zones.

questions.title: Which activities belong in the first month?
questions.context: Select any activities worth trying. We can start with a small program and learn from who turns up.

options.label: Open reading afternoons
options.description: Regular drop-in hours with no program or booking. Visitors bring a book or browse the shelves.
options.benefit: Easy to run and welcoming to people with different schedules.
options.tradeoff: People may need another reason to make their first visit.

options.label: A monthly book circle
options.description: One book, a small group, and a hosted discussion. Announce the book early so people have time to read.
options.benefit: Gives returning visitors a shared interest and a familiar rhythm.
options.tradeoff: Reading the book in advance asks for a bigger commitment.

options.label: Neighbor-led skill sharing
options.description: Short informal sessions such as mending, drawing, or writing, led by people from the neighborhood.
options.benefit: Brings in people who might not join a reading group.
options.tradeoff: Requires finding hosts, preparing materials, and rearranging the room.

questions.title: After three months, what would make this feel worthwhile?
questions.context: Describe one or two things you would hope to notice. A small, specific sign is more useful than a perfect target.
